archetype.name: mature photosynthetic leaf mesophyll cell
archetype.scopeNote: A representative angiosperm leaf cell chosen because the requested combination of a large central vacuole and grana-bearing chloroplasts is characteristic of photosynthetic vegetative tissue. It is not a universal template for every plant cell or tissue.
archetype.requiredInterpretation: The model must read as a cut through a closed three-dimensional cell volume, not as organelles drawn on a flat plate. Every membrane-bounded structure must have depth, an enclosing surface, and a coherent interior.
archetype.neighborContext: Include a small adjacent-cell/wall fragment only where needed to make plasmodesmata anatomically meaningful.

globalConstraints.requirement: Cell wall is the outer extracellular shell; plasma membrane is a distinct, much thinner continuous boundary immediately inside it.
A single membrane-bounded central vacuole dominates the interior and displaces most cytoplasm and organelles to a peripheral layer, while allowing a few plausible transvacuolar cytoplasmic strands.
No organelle may float inside the vacuolar lumen. The tonoplast must separate vacuolar lumen from cytoplasm everywhere except at the deliberate cut surface.
Cut surfaces must expose shell thickness and internal depth. Uncut rear and side surfaces must remain modeled and inspectable through a full orbit.

Use coherent relative scale and spatial relationships. Ultrastructural details that cannot be shown at the same scale may be enlarged only as declared didactic exaggerations, never presented as literal scale.

structures.label: Cell wall
structures.geometry: Rigid, continuous, volumetric outer shell with visible cut thickness; gently faceted or box-like is acceptable for a generalized mesophyll cell.
relationships: Outside the plasma membrane
Shared wall context may be shown at the plasmodesmata patch
avoid: Cell wall drawn inside the plasma membrane
Claiming lignified secondary wall for this generalized living mesophyll cell

structures.label: Plasma membrane
structures.geometry: Thin continuous volumetric surface immediately inside the cell wall and outside the cytoplasm; separation may be visually exaggerated for legibility.
relationships: Encloses the protoplast
Continuous with the outer membrane lining of plasmodesmata
avoid: Leaving it absent at the rear or sides

structures.label: Cytoplasm
structures.geometry: A connected peripheral volume between plasma membrane and tonoplast, with optional narrow transvacuolar strands; not a solid fill occupying the vacuole.
relationships: Contains nucleus and organelles
Continuous around the vacuole and through transvacuolar strands
avoid: Uniformly filling the full cell interior
Treating cytoplasm as only a background color

structures.label: Large central vacuole
structures.geometry: One dominant, fluid-filled three-dimensional compartment. Target roughly 65-85% of model cell volume to preserve the biologically dominant appearance while keeping organelles readable; literature reports up to about 90% in mature vegetative cells.
relationships: Bounded by tonoplast
Pushes nucleus and most organelles toward cell cortex

structures.label: Tonoplast
structures.geometry: A continuous single membrane enclosing the central vacuole, visibly distinct from the plasma membrane.
relationships: Vacuolar lumen on one side
Cytoplasm on the other side

structures.label: Nucleus
structures.geometry: Peripheral, rounded or slightly compressed volumetric organelle with a double nuclear envelope, visible envelope pores only if explicitly marked as enlarged, chromatin-like interior, and one conspicuous nucleolus.
relationships: Located in cytoplasm, not vacuole
Outer nuclear membrane continuous with endoplasmic reticulum
avoid: Central placement that unrealistically displaces the mature vacuole

structures.label: Chloroplasts
structures.geometry: Multiple lenticular or ellipsoidal double-envelope organelles in peripheral cytoplasm. At least one cutaway chloroplast must show stroma and flattened thylakoid membranes arranged in several grana stacks, with intergranal/stroma lamellae connecting stacks.
relationships: Restricted to cytoplasm
Often apposed near the cell periphery
May be near mitochondria and peroxisomes
avoid: Drawing grana as free coins unconnected to thylakoid membrane
Folding the chloroplast inner envelope into cristae

structures.label: Mitochondria
structures.geometry: Several smaller ovoid or short tubular double-membrane organelles. At least one cutaway must show the inner membrane folding inward as cristae around the matrix.
relationships: Located in cytoplasm
May occur near chloroplasts and peroxisomes in photosynthetic tissue

structures.label: Endoplasmic reticulum
structures.geometry: A connected membrane network combining tubules and flattened cisternal regions, distributed through peripheral cytoplasm and optional transvacuolar strands. Rough ER bears cytosolic ribosome particles; smooth ER lacks them.
relationships: Continuous with outer nuclear membrane
Closely associated with dispersed Golgi stacks but not fused into them

structures.label: Golgi apparatus
structures.geometry: Multiple small, dispersed stacks of curved flattened cisternae with nearby vesicles. A visible stack should have an ordered cis-to-trans progression without implying that all stacks form one perinuclear mammalian-style ribbon.
relationships: Dispersed and motile in plant-cell cytoplasm
Functionally associated with ER and trans-Golgi network

structures.label: Ribosomes
structures.geometry: Small particles represented both free in cytosol and attached to the cytosolic face of rough ER; particle size must be flagged as exaggerated if individually visible.
relationships: Free ribosomes in cytosol
Bound ribosomes on rough ER
Organelle ribosomes need not be individually modeled
avoid: Ribosomes embedded between cell wall layers

structures.label: Peroxisomes
structures.geometry: A few small single-membrane spherical to ellipsoidal organelles with a relatively uniform lumen; no cristae, grana, or DNA-bearing double envelope.
relationships: Located in cytoplasm
At least one may be positioned near a chloroplast and mitochondrion to reflect photorespiratory association
avoid: Treating a peroxisome as a miniature vacuole

structures.label: Plasmodesmata
structures.geometry: A localized group of narrow channels traversing the cell wall. For a magnified cutaway, show an outer lining continuous with plasma membrane, a central desmotubule continuous with ER, and a cytosolic sleeve between them.
relationships: Must connect cytoplasm of the modeled cell to an indicated neighboring-cell cytoplasm
Passes through, rather than terminating within, the shared wall
avoid: Literal-scale claim when enlarged for visibility
structures.fallback: If mobile geometry cannot resolve the channel, show a scientifically placed wall patch and a separate labeled magnified inset; do not fabricate a large cellular tunnel.

labelingRules: Use 'cell wall' and 'plasma membrane' as separate labels.
Use 'central vacuole' for the lumen/compartment and 'tonoplast' only for its bounding membrane.
Use 'chloroplast' for the organelle, 'granum' for one stack (plural 'grana'), and 'thylakoid' for the individual/continuous membrane system.
Use 'mitochondrion' for one organelle (plural 'mitochondria') and 'crista' for one inner-membrane fold (plural 'cristae').
Use 'nuclear envelope' for the double membrane and 'nucleolus' for the dense body inside the nucleus.
Do not label generic transport vesicles as lysosomes; the central lytic vacuole fulfills many analogous degradative roles in mature plant cells.
Any enlarged membrane thickness, ribosome, pore, plasmodesma, granum, or crista must be described as a didactic scale exaggeration.
prohibitedMisconceptions: The cell wall replaces the plasma membrane.
The vacuole is empty space or extracellular space.
Grana and mitochondrial cristae are interchangeable structures.
Plasmodesmata are open holes with no membrane continuity.
A representative cell has fixed organelle counts or universally fixed proportions.
acceptanceChecks: A 360-degree orbit confirms closed three-dimensional rear, side, top, and bottom geometry.
The cutaway visibly preserves the outside-to-inside order: cell wall, plasma membrane, cytoplasm, tonoplast, vacuolar lumen.
No chloroplast, mitochondrion, ER, Golgi stack, ribosome, peroxisome, or nucleus intersects or occupies the vacuolar lumen.
One chloroplast cutaway distinguishes double envelope, stroma, grana, and connecting thylakoid lamellae.
One mitochondrion cutaway distinguishes outer membrane, inner membrane/cristae, intermembrane space, and matrix.
Nucleolus is inside a double-envelope nucleus, and ER continuity is spatially credible.
Golgi stacks are dispersed in cytoplasm and composed of stacked cisternae.
If plasmodesmata are present, they cross a shared wall into adjacent-cell context and are declared enlarged.
All labels point to the correct three-dimensional structure without crossing to a different compartment.
Scale legend separates cell-scale geometry from enlarged ultrastructural details.
